Share a file: anyone with its link opens it in the hosted viewer, and downloads the files that made it (the link's .zip, which `cad import` writes into a folder), with no sign-in, until 7 days after its last share. FILE is a CAD file the viewer opens; a model is shared by its .xbf. What goes is the file, the files that made it -- a model's script, the modules of its project that it imports and the files it reads, as its .xbf records them (run it again after an edit); a robot description's mesh files; a KiCad board's or schematic's project file, local libraries, 3D models and sheets -- and its view: its shapes as meshes with their names, measurements and joints, a board's layers in 2D (its 3D is a GLB of its own: `cad export BOARD board.glb`, then share that), a schematic's sheets. Never an installed library. Sharing it again keeps the link and sends only what changed. The first share on a computer needs the person's yes (--yes). `status` says whether sharing is on and lists this computer's live shares; `on` and `off` turn it on and off; `delete` removes a share.
a CAD file the viewer opens (a model's .xbf; a folder has no bundle to share); or status, on, off or delete

cad installs every newer release by itself. `cad update` updates cad now to the newest release, even with automatic updates off: cad asks PyPI, and uv, which installed it, upgrades cad in place. By itself, cad updates as the server next starts once a newer release is out. `cad update auto` shows or changes whether cad updates itself.
